1) The polypeptide chain synthesis rate is the same in growing and amino acid-starved cells of the same genotype.

1) the rate of polypeptide chain synthesis is 2--5 residues per second in amino acid-starvation, compared to 15--30 residues per second during growth, and that this rate difference is independent of the rel+ or rel- state of the cells, and that 2) the rate of chain elongation is the same in growing cells and in amino acid-starvated cells.

the rel+ state is characterized by a more rapid rate of protein synthesis and a more rapid rate and/or extent of ribosomal recycling.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of peptide synthesis is reduced during amino acid starvation, and this is a common feature for both rel- cells and rel+ cells.
the growth rate of peptide chains is decreased in amino acid-starvation conditions, but not by the rel+ phenotype.
the growth rate in amino-acid-starved E. coli is about one-tenth that in growing cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of protein chain growth in amino acid-starving cells is very slow.
the rate of polypeptide chain elongation is much slower in amino acid-starving cells than in growing cells.
the peptide chain growth rates in amino acid-starving cells are much slower than in growing cells.
